headline: RBI imposes monetary penalty on Progfin Private Limited
claimText: RBI imposes monetary penalty on Progfin Private Limited. headline: The Tribunal Rules, 2021 contradict the Supreme Court rulings
claimText: The Tribunal Rules, 2021 contradict the Supreme Court rulings. Supreme Court rulings (1986, 2014, 2019) mandate that tribunals supplanting High Courts must have the same independence and judicial experience as High Courts, and that the Executive should not administer them; the 2021 Ordinance and Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2021, replicated provisions struck down by the Court, including a four‑year term for members and central government control of leave and appointments; the Bill is currently challenged in the Supreme Court for violating these principles.

headline: Understanding vacancies in the Indian judiciary
claimText: Understanding vacancies in the Indian judiciary. Supreme Court collegium has recommended 11 judges for High Courts, but appointments have been delayed; vacancy rates rose from 18% to 21% (Supreme Court 6% to 12%, High Courts 33% to 38%, subordinate courts 18% to 20%) between 2010‑2020, contributing to 4 crore pending cases. As of 1 Nov 2021, the Supreme Court had 1 vacancy out of 34 sanctioned posts; High Courts had 37% vacancies (406/1,098) and subordinate courts 21% vacancies (5,146/24,018) as of 20 Feb 2020, with average appointment time 5‑7 months after collegium recommendation. Law Commission and NCMS propose judge‑to‑population ratio (50 per million) and weighted case‑load methods to calculate optimal judge strength and reduce backlog.

headline: Assam’s new cattle preservation law
claimText: Assam’s new cattle preservation law. The Assam Legislative Assembly passed the Assam Cattle Preservation Bill, 2021, which prohibits the slaughter of cows of all ages and allows the slaughter of bulls or bullocks only if they are over 14 years old or permanently incapacitated. The Bill permits inter‑state and intra‑state transport of cattle only for agricultural or animal‑husbandry purposes with a permit, and restricts transport through Assam unless such a permit is obtained. Sale of beef is allowed only at locations authorized by the competent authority and is barred within a five‑kilometre radius of any temple or in areas predominantly inhabited by non‑beef‑eating communities, a restriction that could effectively prohibit beef sales across most towns in Assam.

claimText: नवगठित राष्ट्रीय अल्पसंख्यक आयोग ने वर्ष 2026 की अपनी पहली बैठक में अल्पसंख्यक समुदायों के कल्याण और सुरक्षा उपायों की समीक्षा की. The newly constituted National Minority Commission, under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, held its inaugural meeting on 20 Aug 2026 in Delhi, chaired by Chairman Harjeet Singh Grewal, with Vice‑Chairperson Ms S Munvari Begam, members Barjis Desai, Glen E Suja Tikalo, Secretary Suchindra Mishra, Joint Secretary Dr Atia Nand and other officials in attendance. During the meeting the commission reviewed the welfare and security measures for minority communities, discussed ongoing activities, pending issues and charted strategies for further action. Chairman Grewal reiterated the commission’s mandate to monitor and implement security measures for the protection and development of minorities.

headline: Seven years of Swachh Bharat Mission
claimText: Seven years of Swachh Bharat Mission. Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 Oct 2014 with the vision of a clean India by 2 Oct 2019, aiming to eliminate open defecation, eradicate manual scavenging and promote scientific solid‑waste management.

headline: Explained: Karnataka’s Ordinance on religious conversion
claimText: Explained: Karnataka’s Ordinance on religious conversion. Karnataka Protection of Right to Freedom of Religion Ordinance, 2022 prohibits forced conversions through misrepresentation, coercion, allurement, fraud or marriage promise. Penalties include 3–10 years imprisonment and fines up to Rs 1 lakh, with cognizable non‑bailable offences. Conversion requires pre‑ and post‑conversion declarations to the District Magistrate, a 30‑day objection period and possible enquiry.

headline: Explained: Draft amendments to the IT Rules 2021
claimText: Explained: Draft amendments to the IT Rules 2021. On 6 June 2022, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology released draft amendments to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 for public feedback. The draft proposes a Grievance Appellate Committee, chaired by a person appointed by the central government, to hear appeals against grievance officers and to dispose of such appeals within 30 days. The amendments tighten timelines for removing prohibited content, mandating that complaints be addressed within 72 hours, compared with the earlier 24‑hour acknowledgment and 15‑day disposal requirement.

headline: Explained: Role of Governor in Public Universities
claimText: Explained: Role of Governor in Public Universities. West Bengal University Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2022 replaces Governor with Chief Minister as Chancellor of 31 state public universities, shifting headship and convocation duties. Supreme Court 1997 held Governor not bound by aid and advice of Council of Ministers while acting as Chancellor; Sarkaria and Poonch Commission recommended limiting Governor’s statutory powers. Tamil Nadu (2022) and Maharashtra (2021) bills transfer Vice‑Chancellor appointment from Governor to state government, tightening state control over higher‑education governance.

headline: Lok Sabha passes a Bill to regulate doping in sports
claimText: Lok Sabha passes a Bill to regulate doping in sports. The National Anti‑Doping Bill, 2021, passed by Lok Sabha, makes the National Anti‑Doping Agency (NADA) a statutory body headed by a Director General appointed by the central government. It establishes a National Anti‑Doping Disciplinary Panel and an Appeal Panel to adjudicate violations, and introduces sanctions such as disqualification, ineligibility, and financial penalties. The Bill addresses concerns over NADA’s independence, athlete privacy, and testing capacity, and aligns India’s anti‑doping framework with the World Anti‑Doping Code.

headline: Inflation targets not met – MPC to examine today
claimText: Inflation targets not met – MPC to examine today. The policy repo rate was raised progressively from 4% in April 2022 to 5.9% in September 2022 to curb inflation.

headline: How India will elect its next President
claimText: How India will elect its next President. The President is elected by an electoral college of elected MPs and MLAs of the states and the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry, as prescribed in Article 55 of the Constitution. Each MLA’s vote value is based on the state’s 1971 population and the number of MLAs (e.g., UP MLA = 208, Sikkim MLA = 7); an MP’s vote value equals the total MLA vote value divided by the number of elected MPs, resulting in a value of 700 in 2022. A candidate must be proposed and seconded by at least 50 elected representatives and must deposit Rs 15,000 as security, a requirement introduced by the 1997 amendment.

headline: Result of the Second Overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction held on August 20, 2026
claimText: Result of the Second Overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction held on August 20, 2026. The RBI conducted the second overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction on 20 August 2026 with a notified amount of ₹50,000 crore and total offers of ₹53,938 crore, of which ₹50,013 crore were accepted. The auction’s cut‑off and weighted‑average rate were both 5.24 % and 92.7 % of offers were accepted at the cut‑off rate.

headline: स्टील अथॉरिटी ऑफ इण्डिया लिमिटेड (SAIL) ने एमएमडीआर संशोधन अधिनियम, 2026 का किया स्वागत, बताया खनिज सुरक्षा और घरेलू लौह अयस्क की उपलब्धता बढ़ाने की दिशा में बड़ा सुधार
claimText: स्टील अथॉरिटी ऑफ इण्डिया लिमिटेड (SAIL) ने एमएमडीआर संशोधन अधिनियम, 2026 का किया स्वागत, बताया खनिज सुरक्षा और घरेलू लौह अयस्क की उपलब्धता बढ़ाने की दिशा में बड़ा सुधार. SAIL welcomed the Mineral (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026 announced on 17 August 2026, calling it a step that provides an estimated financial framework and long‑term policy certainty for the mineral sector. The amendment introduces clearer, uniform mineral taxes and fees, resolves pending tax cases, and is expected to boost confidence, attract new investment, facilitate development of SAIL’s large captive iron‑ore and coal mines, and strengthen long‑term raw‑material security. By enabling better mine development, the reform should increase domestic iron‑ore availability, allow SAIL to sell additional ore under the new rules, strengthen the Indian steel supply chain, reduce import dependence and enhance the competitiveness of mineral‑based industries, aligning with the ‘Atmanirbhar’ and ‘Developed India’ objectives.

headline: How long can the central government take to frame Rules?
claimText: How long can the central government take to frame Rules?. Ordinarily, Rules, Regulations and bye‑laws must be framed within six months from the date on which the concerned Act came into force. If the six‑month period expires, the Ministry must seek an extension from the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, stating the reason; such extensions may be granted for a maximum of three months at a time. An extension was granted for framing Rules under the Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019 on account of the COVID‑19 pandemic.

headline: Anti-cheating laws for competitive examinations
claimText: Anti-cheating laws for competitive examinations. Over the past few years, states such as Uttarakhand, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and others have enacted specific anti‑cheating Acts covering public service recruitment exams and, in many cases, school/college examinations. The statutes prescribe imprisonment (from three months in UP to seven years in AP) and debarment (typically two to five years), with Uttarakhand’s 2023 Act uniquely allowing debarment upon filing of a chargesheet rather than conviction. These laws also criminalise paper leaks, impersonation and the use of electronic aids, aiming to safeguard the integrity of competitive examinations.

headline: First no-confidence motion of the 17th Lok Sabha discussed today
claimText: First no-confidence motion of the 17th Lok Sabha discussed today. Article 75(3) mandates collective responsibility of the government to Lok Sabha; a no‑confidence motion requires support of at least 50 members and is debated within 10 days. Since 1952, 28 no‑confidence motions and 11 confidence motions have been discussed; none have forced a government to resign except the 1979 inconclusive case. The 2023 motion was debated for 12 hours over 13 days, illustrating procedural norms and the rarity of successful trust votes.

headline: What is Fuelling Power Sector Losses?
claimText: What is Fuelling Power Sector Losses?. State‑owned power distribution companies incurred Rs 68,832 crore losses in 2022‑23, quadrupling 2021‑22 losses, largely due to rising coal import costs and high generation expenses. Coal imports rose 27 million tonnes in 2022‑23, with price increasing 51 % from Rs 8,300 to Rs 12,500 per tonne, driven by the Russia‑Ukraine war and global demand. Discoms face structural issues: long‑term power purchase agreements lock in high costs, delayed subsidies create cash‑flow constraints, and tariffs are revised infrequently, leading to persistent financial deficits.
